Per Atlas 6552087494 (Muse 6552134028): a module wrapper (top-level immediately-invoked function, named or anonymous, and a factory passed to it) is module scope, so protection does not depend on wrapper syntax; each reached module has a residual pin over everything outside its function definitions (wrapper glue, the export table, module-scope data, top-level statements), with whitespace normalised outside literals only; module-scope data that pinned code names is also pinned; whole-module pin where the module cannot be parsed, where none of its functions execute under the declared states, or where it registers callbacks the capture never invokes and its handlers are not modelled by the state matrix (STATE_MODELLED in test/lib/savings-consumer-contract.js); each page's script list and HTML bytes and the capture, collector, validator, poster and guard machinery are pinned.
uncovered: Unexecuted branches and helpers inside function-level modules (outside the selector region and the reached set) remain the declared unexecuted-path limit, covered by exact-head review only (Muse 6550491885, 6550973450); this is distinct from unresolved reachability, which takes the whole-module fallback (Atlas 6552087494 item 6).
